This valuation suggests that the market anticipates future scale and brand equity that current earnings metrics fail to capture. Despite these figures, the stock is currently trading at only 42% of its 52-week range [E3], providing an entry point that does not reflect the aggressive valuation the market has already assigned to the company's book value [E5]. The current market capitalization of ₹ 4,328 Cr [E1] represents a valuation that prioritizes the company's asset base over its recent, volatile return metrics [E11, E16].

The bull’s reliance on a 4.04x P/B ratio [E5] as a signal of confidence is fundamentally flawed when contrasted with the company’s catastrophic return metrics. While the bull interprets this premium as intangible value, it is more accurately viewed as an overvaluation of assets that are failing to generate any meaningful return, evidenced by a staggering ROE of -513% [E11, E16] and a median 3-year ROE of -176% [E15, E35]. Conceded: the company trades at 42% of its 52-week range [E3] and carries a P/B ratio higher than the sector benchmark [E5]. However, this premium is disconnected from reality given the ROA of -38.8% [E6] and a ROCE of -12.4% [E10], which indicate that the capital deployed is actively destroying value rather than building it. The bull’s dismissal of the 0x P/E ratio [E4] ignores that the company lacks the positive earnings necessary to justify its ₹ 4,328 Cr market capitalization [E1]. Ultimately, the market’s pricing of the book value is not a sign of growth potential, but a reflection of a business model that has consistently failed to produce a positive return on equity [E37].
